title: SO-F-04B One Admission per scope: an AdmissionSet that holds the Admissions of a node's scopes, refuses a second Admission for a scope through a registry kept for the log, and routes a contribution to the Admission of its scope
request: Follow-up to the signed SO-F-04, written from the open follow-up row 'One scope per Admission' of docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md (Admission, SO-F-04, pull request #368). Unsigned: a delta proposed for red-team review. It does not supersede SO-F-04 and does not edit it; it depends on SO-F-03.4, proposed in the same pull request, which supersedes the signed SO-F-03.3 and owns the replay mark. The id has no '.N' suffix because in this repository a '.N' id is a superseding version; this is an additive follow-up, as SO-W-08C is to SO-W-08B. OWNER DECISION (1 Nov 2026, on pull request #374): the sequence is per sender and scope, matching one Admission per scope, on condition that the scope is bound inside the signed envelope. PRECONDITION, CHECKED: the scope is bound in the signed bytes. At 042d727, contributionMessage in src/engine/federation/contribution.mjs (line 67) is the text that is signed: a header line and the canonical text of the whole envelope without its content hash and without the signature, so extension.contribution.scope, the sequence, the subject and the node (origin.node) are all inside the signed bytes; signContribution (line 85) signs that text. No test of SO-F-03 proves the scope part (the test at test/federation-admission.test.mjs:226 to 228 proves it for the payload hash only), so a criterion of SO-F-03.4 does. If the signed text ever stops covering the scope, a mark per sender and scope is not safe and the stop rules apply. RELATION TO SO-F-03.3, FLAGGED: SO-F-03.3 (signed) says the sequence is per sender (its request, requirement and criterion 2: 'the per-sender high-water mark is persisted through the operation log and rebuilt on open'), docs/FEDERATION.md line 224 says the same, and test/federation-admission.test.mjs keys the mark by the sender alone (highWater('node-01|agent:writer')). A mark per sender and scope therefore differs from the signed text. An earlier draft of this contract kept the SO-F-03.3 per-sender mark for a lone Admission and gave the set a mark of its own; the red-team showed that this could not be seeded safely and left a bare Admission over the log able to admit a sequence twice. The rule is therefore moved to its root: SO-F-03.4 supersedes SO-F-03.3 openly (the criterion that said per sender is superseded by name, the five SO-F-03 tests it selects stay green and are not edited, and the Admission reads the log again when it has moved), and this contract keeps no mark of its own. RED-TEAM RESPONSE (1 Nov 2026): the set no longer shares a mark, so add() has nothing to seed and nothing to merge; an Admission that admitted sequence 7 before it was added, one added to two sets and two sets over one log are covered by the Admission's own re-read of the log (SO-F-03.4) and by a registry kept for the log. The word 'enforced' of the earlier draft overclaimed: the set refuses a second Admission among the Admissions it is given, and it cannot refuse a bare new Admission(...) it is never told of. That is safe for replay because every Admission reads the log (SO-F-03.4); a scan criterion pins that no module under src builds an Admission but admission.mjs, so that nothing in the product builds a second Admission behind the set. A second Admission with a policy of its own would still answer by that policy; that is not a replay matter and is not closed here. MERGE ORDER of the three specs of pull request #374, which touch the same files. Spec pull requests: #374 changes contracts/scope-one/manifest.json, docs/scope-one/RECONCILIATION.md and docs/scope-one/WBS.md the way every spec-only pull request does, by adding rows and, for a superseded contract, two fields, so it and the other open spec pull request that does the same (SO-F-09.3, #373) take a plain merge of main in whichever order they land, keeping both sets of rows; no spec depends on that order. Build order: pull requests #358 (SO-F-03.3) and #368 (SO-F-04) first; then SO-F-03.4 (admission.mjs: the mark and the re-read; docs/FEDERATION.md, the paragraph that says per sender); then SO-F-04B, which needs SO-F-03.4 (admission.mjs: AdmissionSet, one registration in the constructor, one shared function for a rejected record); SO-F-04A depends on neither and may be built before or after (admission.mjs: composeExternal only). Each of the three edits src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, docs/FEDERATION.md, docs/MODULES.md and test/helpers/** in a different place, and the one built later merges the one built earlier. Sign order: SO-F-03.4 before SO-F-04B; SO-F-04A at any time. BASE: SO-F-04. The files this contract names are in pull request #368 (head 042d727: relationshipGate, RelationshipBook, test/helpers/federation-node.mjs), which was not merged when this was written, and in src/engine/federation/admission.mjs (SO-F-03.3), which is on main since pull request #358 merged (the copy on main is the same file as at 042d727, the commit I read); SO-F-03.4 is a spec that is not built. Draft, red-team and sign this contract against a base that holds pull request #368 and SO-F-03.4, and build it after they land; on main today the named test cannot load its helper and the check cannot run. This pull request is spec only. WHAT THE CODE DOES TODAY (read, and run in a scratch script outside the repository, at 042d727): an Admission takes one scope and refuses a contribution for any other at the authority step with the code scope_mismatch, so a node with several relationships needs one Admission per scope, as the pull request body says. Four things follow that nothing states or checks. (1) Nothing stops a second Admission for the same scope over the same log. Two such Admissions each admitted sequence 5 of the same sender, and the log holds two federation.admitted records for it: the mark is a map in memory, read from the log when the Admission is made and never again. SO-F-03.4 closes that. (2) The mark is per sender across all scopes and is rebuilt from every federation.admitted record whatever its scope, so with one Admission per scope over one log whether a sequence is a replay depends on when each Admission was made. SO-F-03.4 closes that. (3) test/federation-admission.test.mjs (SO-F-03 AC04) builds a second Admission for the scope a first one holds, over the same log object, to show that membership changes the answer. A refusal in the Admission constructor would fail that signed contract's test, so no guard can live there, and the registry of this contract lives in the set. (4) An object made with Object.create(Admission.prototype), or one with the same fields, passes instanceof Admission, so instanceof is no test that a value is an Admission. WHAT THIS CONTRACT SPECIFIES: AdmissionSet, exported from src/engine/federation/admission.mjs. new AdmissionSet({ log }) takes the operation log and throws a TypeError for anything that has no append and iterate. add(admission) holds an Admission and throws a TypeError that names the problem when the value is not an Admission, when the Admission's log is not the set's log, or when an Admission for the same scope is already held for this log, by this set or by any other set over the same log. 'Is an Admission' is a brand and not instanceof: the Admission constructor registers each instance it makes in a module-private WeakSet, after all of its existing validation, as its only change (it adds no guard, and changes nothing the constructor accepts, refuses or does), and add accepts only a registered object, so a subclass made through super is accepted and an object made with Object.create(Admission.prototype), or with the same fields, is refused. The registry is a module-private WeakMap keyed by the log object, holding for each log the scopes held and by which set; it is what refuses a second set over one log and an Admission added to two sets (the second add names the scope). A refused add changes neither the set nor the registry. There is no remove: a scope stays held for as long as its log object lives, and a node that opens its vault again has a new log object and a new registry. admit(envelope, options) validates the envelope and routes a contribution to the one Admission whose scope is the contribution's scope. A malformed envelope is refused at the format step. A contribution for a scope no held Admission holds is refused at the authority step with the code scope_mismatch, appended once as federation.rejected with nothing of the payload, before any external check or signature check runs, so no service is called for a scope the node does not hold; its result has signature_valid false, because no signature was checked, and its record does not say otherwise. The set records these refusals through one function that the Admission's own rejected-event writer also uses, so that the record has the same keys as any other federation.rejected record. An AdmissionSet with no Admission is valid: it refuses every well-formed contribution with scope_mismatch and a malformed one at the format step, and its highWater is 0. highWater(sender, scope) of the set is that of the held Admission of the scope, and 0 for a scope none holds. The set keeps no mark of its own: the mark of each Admission is the SO-F-03.4 mark, read from the log, so a sequence is a replay in the same cases through the set, through a held Admission's own admit, for an Admission that admitted before it was added, and after the log is opened again. The set adds no event type and no store, and creates no file; the log is the only store. BOUNDARIES: (1) Two processes over one log are the single-writer rule of SR-1.01, not this contract. (2) Alternatives to the set are listed in the pull request for the owner: an Admission that takes several scopes in one constructor, which is not chosen here, and an Admission that reads the log at each admit, which SO-F-03.4 now specifies. (3) A relationship is the edge between two nodes (SO-F-04); the set holds Admissions by scope and reads no relationship. (4) The registry has no remove and no expiry; whether a set may release a scope is an open question for the owner. Provenance: written for this repository, not adapted from the fold. Settled decisions this contract follows (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md): topology is local-first and the cloud is only a relay and a backup; every supported provider stands on equal footing and no work or tier depends on one; crdt-merge is reached only through the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs and this contract adds no merge engine to the core (ADR 6, decided); tiers follow docs/PRICING.md and federation stays a planned capability of the tiers above Personal, by contacting us, never a price cell. Open decisions this contract does not make: ADR 7 (memory and project-state authority, proposed) is cited and not decided, and this contract adds no store and no event type beyond the two the Admission already writes (federation.admitted and federation.rejected), so there is one store under the vault and no second database; ADR 2 (id and event ordering, open) keeps its safe default, the order of the operation log, and this contract adds no sequence of its own; ADR 3 (lease semantics, open) is not touched, and nothing here is a lease or a role-by-action rule. ADR 5 (permission matrix, open) and SO-A-05 (the decision and blocker queue; the place where an admission decision would be raised, and who may answer one, stays provisional until both are decided) are not touched: nothing here raises a decision or a blocker, and a degraded answer is not one. ADR 8 (trust governance in the federated model, proposed, pending owner decision; docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md and docs/scope-one/design/trust-governance.md) is not decided or pre-empted: nothing here defines a trust record, a trust gate, who may grant trust or how a revocation propagates, and no criterion reads trust.

requirements: AdmissionSet, exported from src/engine/federation/admission.mjs, holds the Admissions of one log, and add refuses, with a TypeError that names the problem, a value that is not an Admission (a brand registered by the constructor, not instanceof), an Admission over another log and a second Admission for a scope already held for the log by this set or any other

a registry kept for the log (a WeakMap keyed by the log object) is what refuses a second set over one log and an Admission added to two sets; a refused add changes neither the set nor the registry; there is no remove

admit validates the envelope and routes a contribution to the one Admission of its scope; a malformed envelope is refused at the format step; a scope that no held Admission holds, including every scope of an empty set, is refused once at the authority step with the code scope_mismatch, before any external check or signature check, with signature_valid false and a record that does not claim a verified signature

the set keeps no mark of its own: a sequence is a replay in the same cases through the set, through a held Admission's own admit, for an Admission that admitted before it was added, and after the log is opened again, because each Admission holds the mark per sender and scope of SO-F-03.4; highWater(sender, scope) of the set reads it and is 0 for a scope none holds

a message replayed into a different scope is refused through the set at the signature step (the scope is inside the signed bytes), one aimed at a scope no held Admission holds is refused with scope_mismatch, and the original sent again to its own scope is a replay

a lone Admission and a set holding one Admission give the same results and the same events for the same contributions, and the set adds no event type, no store and no file; two scopes with two relationships under the gates of SO-F-04 are admitted and refused each on its own relationship, and one revocation leaves the other
no module under src builds an Admission but admission.mjs, so that nothing in the product builds a second Admission behind a set

docs/FEDERATION.md states that a node holds one Admission per scope in an AdmissionSet, that a second for the same scope is refused when it is added, through a registry kept for the log, that a bare Admission over the log is not refused by the set and is safe for replay because every Admission reads the log (SO-F-03.4), and that the set keeps no mark
tasks.description: A node with several relationships has several scopes, and the Admission holds one. This contract makes the arrangement explicit: one Admission per scope, held in one set that routes a contribution to the Admission of its scope, so that adding a second Admission for a scope is an error at the moment it is added, wherever the second one is added. The replay answer does not depend on the set: each Admission holds the mark per sender and scope of SO-F-03.4, so what the set must not do is keep a second mark that could disagree with the log. The set does not claim to stop a bare Admission built behind it; it pins that nothing in src builds one. It leaves the choice of a different design (several scopes in one Admission, a release of a scope from the registry) to the owner. The named test imports each module of the contract by namespace (import * as ns), never by name, and asserts that the export it needs is a function or a class before it uses it, so that on the base the red run fails on an assertion; the red-green check treats a load error as BLOCKED, not as red.

stop_rules: Stop and post BLOCKED when a criterion cannot pass without weakening a test, skipping a test or relaxing an assertion.
Stop and ask when the work would name a client product, a person, a server or a seat in repository text; the client names live in docs/CLIENTS.md only.
Stop when the work would add a runtime dependency, a model call, a network call at install or start, a second store for project state, or any reporting that is not opt-in and off by default.
